title: Withdraw your application to register your relationship
summary: This page explains how to withdraw an application to register a relationship with the NSW Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages.
intro:
Couples who are in a relationship, but not married, can apply to register a relationship with NSW Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages.

You or the other adult can withdraw the application, however, you will need to do this within 28 days of applying.

### Fees

There is no fee to withdraw an application.

Note: the original application fee is non-refundable.
who_can_apply: Couples who have applied to register a relationship with NSW Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages.
what_you_need: Copies of your proof of identity documents
Withdraw a relationship registration application form

how_to_steps.text: Bring your original proof of identity documents.
Visit a service centre and submit your withdraw a relationship registration application form.
Make copies of your proof of identity documents.
Post your application form and proof of identity copies to the address on the form.Note: do not send original documents.

faqs.q: How long do I have to withdraw my application?
faqs.a: You must withdraw the application within 28 days of applying.

faqs.q: Are there any fees to withdraw the application?
faqs.a: There is no fee to withdraw an application, but the original application fee is non-refundable.

faqs.q: What do I need to do to withdraw my application?
faqs.a: You can either visit a service centre or post your application form and copies of your proof of identity documents.
